question: What does the 2014-2016 Agusan Marsh fishery assessment establish, and can its landing-center records be assigned as species presence to individual marsh waters or current locations?

source.citation: Baclayo, J. M., Alcantara, M. T., Holoyohoy, L. M., and Alaba, L. A. (2020). Status of Fisheries in Agusan Marsh: Lapaz and Talacogon, Agusan del Sur, Mindanao. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 27(1), 54-82. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/27.1.2019C0002
source.access: The official NFRDI journal article record, repository metadata and publisher-hosted full-text PDF were reviewed. No source table, figure, map or coordinate is reproduced or retained.

studyContext.waterbodyAsReported: Agusan Marsh, with fishery monitoring in Lapaz and Talacogon, Agusan del Sur
studyContext.fieldPeriod: The reported fishery monitoring period is May 2014 through December 2016.
studyContext.samplingFrame: The study describes four monitored fishery landing centers in Lapaz and Talacogon. The article reports fishery catch and composition, not a standardized whole-marsh ecological census.
studyContext.geographicResolution: The catch-composition table aggregates results by municipality (Lapaz and Talacogon). The reviewed paper does not link each taxon to a specific landing center, capture waterbody feature, or capture coordinate. A landing center is not a fish capture origin.
studyContext.taxonomicAndCountScope: The paper reports 18 species and its Table 3 contains 18 status-labeled rows, but one row is Macrobrachium spp., a genus-level freshwater prawn label rather than a fish species. The table also prints Trichopodus pectoralis and Trichogaster pectoralis in separate rows, and the source varies between Osphronemus laticlavius and O. lacticlavius. These source labels are preserved as unresolved; no row-by-row taxonomic crosswalk was performed.
studyContext.municipalRichness: The article reports 12 recorded species in Lapaz and 17 in Talacogon. These municipal figures are not additive and do not identify species-specific capture sites.
studyContext.dietAndHabitat: The article discusses seasonal and flood-related context and cites separate historical feeding literature, but this fishery assessment does not supply a taxon-by-food gut-content result suitable for a diet card or bait recommendation.
studyContext.license: The current TPJF publication policy says submitted articles are licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. The reviewed 2020 article PDF and repository item metadata did not display an item-specific license notice, and applicability of the current policy to this article was not independently confirmed. Treat item-level reuse as unverified pending clarification.

countAudit.note: The 18-row table includes Macrobrachium spp., which is a crustacean and only genus-rank label, so it does not independently substantiate 18 fish species. The municipality-level richness values describe overlapping catches and are not summed. The source also has unresolved name duplication/spelling differences; no unique modern taxon count was calculated.

interpretation.safeSummary: This is a historical primary fisheries assessment based on 2014-2016 monitored landings from four centers in Lapaz and Talacogon. Its catch-composition output is aggregated by municipality and does not resolve taxon-specific capture origin within Agusan Marsh. The claimed fish-species total also includes a genus-level prawn row and unresolved source-name variants.
notSupported: Current presence, abundance, catchability, safe harvest, or a complete present-day Agusan Marsh checklist.
Assigning any named taxon to a particular marsh lake, river channel, landing center, or mapped capture point.
Treating every Table 3 row as a distinct fish species or treating the source's native/introduced labels as current taxonomic or conservation status.
Species-specific diet, prey, bait recommendations, current water quality, safety, or current fishing rules.
A fish absence conclusion from taxa not appearing in this historical fishery sample.
interpretation.productUseIfEvidenceAndRightsAreResolved: A future research-source note may describe the historical time period, two municipality-level fisheries, four monitored landing centers and unresolved scope. Any waterbody-level species display needs a separate source that establishes the taxon and capture waterbody or reach, followed by current name, provenance and reuse review.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Officially archived primary fisheries assessment with a stated historical period and four monitored landing centers, but municipal aggregation, no taxon-to-capture-origin crosswalk, and fish/species count ambiguity.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: Current TPJF policy states CC BY-NC 4.0 for submitted articles, but the 2020 article copy has no detected item-specific notice and the policy's applicability to this item was not independently verified. No public-app reuse approval is granted.
qualityAndRights.handling: This file records a short attributed audit only. It does not reproduce the species table, abundance figures, photographs, map or coordinates. No source PDF is retained and no public app row is admitted.
qualityAndRights.separateEvidenceLanes: Historical landings remain separate from current occurrence, capture geography, taxonomic identity, natural diet, bait suggestions, water quality, safety and legal fishing guidance.

disposition.reason: The historical landings are aggregated by municipality rather than taxon-specific capture waterbody, and the nominal species list includes a genus-level prawn plus unresolved name variants. Item-specific application of reuse terms remains unverified.

nextAction: Continue the Caraga inland source sweep with a taxon-by-station primary survey or a voucher-linked dataset that distinguishes freshwater marsh, lake and river sites. Do not use landing-center records as capture coordinates or current occurrence rows.

sources.supports: Official NFRDI journal article metadata, citation, DOI and abstract-level study period and reported summary.
Full article methods, four monitored landing centers, 2014-2016 period, municipality-level catch tables, source taxon labels and catch-scope limitations.
Official NFRDI repository record and archival metadata.
Current TPJF publication-policy statement that submitted manuscripts are licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0; not confirmation of item-specific applicability to the 2020 article.
